text:
julia: heads-up — seeing a sharp spike in tiny-gpu pool churn in us-west2 around 08:13. dozens of small pods pending for >2m, then cluster-autoscaler/warmpool triggers drains, evicts, then immediately reschedules same pods causing a churn loop.

julia: sample `kubectl get pods -o wide` from node-az3: 
```
NAME                        READY STATUS   NODE         RESTARTS AGE
training-job-abc-12         0/1   Pending    <none>       0       3m
inference-lite-45           0/1   Pending    <none>       0       4m
```

kevin: noticed the same alerts. spike in evictions + node-drain-jobs. Cloud events show a batch of preemptible reclamations in us-west2b at 08:11, then warmpool scaled up in us-west2c. weird rack/az mismatch.

omar: can you paste the drain job logs? my hunch: warmpool instances are coming up with a taint or different labels (rack/az-locality) so scheduler packs differently and descheduler tries to rebalance -> cascading evicts. also autoscaler might be doing immediate drains when warmpool becomes available.

julia: paste of the drain controller snippet: 
```
I0314 08:12:03 drain-controller] starting drain for node node-az3-xx (reason: warmpool-scale)
I0314 08:12:04 drain-controller] cordon node-az3-xx
I0314 08:12:05 drain-controller] evicting 12 pods, parallelism=10
I0314 08:12:45 drain-controller] drain finished, deprovision= true
```

lina: FYI rebalancer bot also posted multiple orphaned-slot fixes around same time: `s-rebalancer-bot: moved 8 tiny pods to node-az2-yy` then `autoscaler-bot: removed node node-az2-yy (scale-down)` 30s later.

omar: yep that sequence matches a backpressure cascade: 1) spot reclaim in azB -> autoscaler tries to move load to warmpool in azC 2) warmpool nodes have different rack labels -> scheduler avoids packing there for some pods with soft-affinity -> descheduler/rebalancer move pods around 3) scale-down sees underutilized nodes and removes them -> pods bounce.

kevin: short-term mitigation idea: pause warmpool-driven drains for 30m in us-west2; throttle drain parallelism to 2; raise warmpool-min to avoid immediate scale-up/down hysteresis. can ops do that quickly?

julia: I can pause the warmpool hook for us-west2 now. also increasing drain-controller `maxParallelEvicts` to 2 in the config.

lina: I'll add a temporary descheduler blocklist for tiny-gpu class to avoid aggressive moves for 1h.

omar: medium-term: two infra changes to prevent recurrence: a) make warmpool instance template carry canonical rack/az labels + same taints as production nodes so scheduler packing doesn't diverge, b) update autoscaler to wait 60s after warmpool attach before initiating drains/evictions (cooldown).

omar: also propose scheduler tweak: for tiny GPU pods (<0.5 gpu) prefer late-binding disabled so they get placed on existing nodes if possible (reduce small-pod scatter). canary rollout to 10% of clusters first.

kevin: cost note: increasing warmpool-min will raise baseline cost ~0.6k/mo for us-west2; still cheaper than repeated preempt evict churn. please include that in the PR.

julia: action items: 
- julia: pause warmpool hook + set maxParallelEvicts=2 (in progress)
- lina: add descheduler blocklist for tiny-gpu class (in progress)
- omar: PR with warmpool-template label parity + autoscaler cooldown (target EOD)
- kevin: post cost delta in the PR and get approval if >$1k/mo

autoscaler-bot: scale events around 08:10-08:15: added 4 warmpool nodes us-west2c, removed 5 preempt nodes us-west2b.

s-rebalancer-bot: moved 12 pods across nodes between 08:12-08:14 (policy=repack).

kevin: once mitigations are live we'll watch eviction rate metric and pending pods. if it stays >5% for >10m we escalate to a live call.

julia: paused warmpool hook — watching. eviction rate dropped from 22% -> 6% in last 90s. will keep monitoring and follow up with root-cause PR. :thumbsup:
